documents.unit: The AI Lab Notebook (Clarkson Documentation Library) / Faculty Senate
documents.title: AI Course Policies
documents.summary: A short Clarkson documentation page recommending that instructors put an AI statement in their syllabus, based on a 2023 Faculty Senate recommendation that was not made mandatory. It links an external crowd-sourced policy collection.
documents.stance_why: The page only "suggests instructors provide a paragraph" in the syllabus and notes the Senate made it "a recommendation instead of a mandate"; it sets no AI rule itself, so it delegates to instructors.

units.why: The university "suggests instructors provide a paragraph outlining the specific guidelines for student use of AI in the course syllabus", a recommendation (should) to instructors made when communicating expectations; P09 fits as it asks for an AI statement in the syllabus, though only as a suggestion.
units.anchor: suggests instructors provide a paragraph outlining the specific guidelines for student use of AI

units.why: The Faculty Senate "endorsed a recommendation to the faculty that they should include a statement in their course syllabi" starting Fall 2023, a dated institutional recommendation about syllabus AI statements; P09 fits, modality should because it is a recommendation.
units.anchor: recommendation to the faculty that they should include a statement in their course syllabi
units.frag_start: the Faculty Senate endorsed a recommendation
units.frag_end: use of AI-driven tools in the course

units.why: "the Senate amended the proposal by making it a recommendation instead of a mandate" states that the syllabus statement is not required; this clarifies the status of the P09 rule (explicitly not a requirement), so the actor is instructors and the modality informs rather than must.
units.anchor: making it a recommendation instead of a mandate
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P04 (each instructor decides); coder B coded P09. Source: 'Please note that the Senate amended the proposal by making it a recommendation instead of a mandate.' It qualifies the syllabus-statement recommendation (P09) rather than saying who sets the AI rule, and a reader looking for the syllabus-statement rule would look under P09. Kept P09, actor instructor, phase general, modality informs (both coders agreed on those).

units.why: The page links a "crowd-sourced list of policies from various institutions" that colleagues may download or share; this is support for faculty drafting course policy, so P63 rather than a stance type, with modality may.
units.anchor: view a crowd-sourced list of policies from various institutions
units.frag_start: Follow the link below to view

documents.title: AI Resources for Faculty
documents.summary: A library guide for faculty stating Clarkson has no institutional AI policy and recommending that instructors define AI usage levels in syllabi. The rest is mostly links to external teaching and AI-literacy resources.
documents.stance_why: The page says "Clarkson does not have an institutional AI policy, instructors are able to determine when and how students should use AI" and offers only syllabus recommendations, so it delegates.

units.why: "Clarkson does not have an institutional AI policy, instructors are able to determine when and how students should use AI" sets no university stance and hands the decision to instructors, so P04 (not P02 or P01).
units.anchor: instructors are able to determine when and how students should use AI

units.why: "Clearly identifying levels of generative AI usage in the syllabus is the best way to maintain consistency" recommends defined levels of AI use, which is P05 (named levels); it is advice, so should.
units.anchor: Clearly identifying levels of generative AI usage in the syllabus is the best way
units.frag_start: Clearly identifying levels of generative AI

units.why: "make expectations very clear and prominently displayed for each assignment or course component" asks instructors to communicate AI rules per assignment; P09 (communicate expectations) fits better than P05 since no levels are named here.
units.anchor: make expectations very clear and prominently displayed for each assignment or course component
units.frag_start: As they may potentially have multiple

units.why: "Defining AI usage levels and providing examples will help students adhere to expectations" recommends defining usage levels with examples; P05 fits, and the examples element is advice to instructors on communicating, so modality should.
units.anchor: Defining AI usage levels and providing examples will help students adhere to expectations
units.frag_start: Defining AI usage levels and providing

units.why: "If you are unfamiliar with generative AI technology, take some time to learn about the tools and how students are using them" advises faculty to learn about AI before deciding policy; this is P63.
units.anchor: take some time to learn about the tools and how students are using them

units.why: "these suggestions can help you integrate generative AI into your courses" offers curriculum suggestions for incorporating AI into assignments; P35 (redesign around AI) fits, as a permissive option (may) addressed to instructors.
units.anchor: these suggestions can help you integrate generative AI into your courses
units.frag_start: Depending on the discipline and specific
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on P35, may, before-course; they differed on unit_stance (A encourage, B neutral) and topics. Source: 'these suggestions can help you integrate generative AI into your courses' offers curriculum suggestions for integrating AI, which takes a position favouring integration, so encourage. Topics merge A's assessment-design with B's instructor-discretion.

notes: Reconciled from two coders who found the same two university-layer documents (AI Course Policies page, Libraries AI Resources for Faculty) and the same 10 units. No school or computing policy found; course layer deferred. The 2025-2026 Student Regulations were fetched and contain no AI mentions. Anchors taken from coder B where shorter or verified verbatim against the cached text.
